name: Question 14
problem:
Let $R=[1,3]\times [1,4]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=x+y.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}={1,2,3},\,{P}_{2}={1,2,3,4},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the lower Riemann sum $L(f,P).$
worked_solution:
First, let's draw the region $R$ and the partition $P.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072149/assets/9b26ea696afda59a7181f062c7c9fab4be373035678eafa0da51bf2b22f9f4b3.png)

The lower sum $L(f,P)$ is given by 

$$
L(f,P)={m}_{11}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{11})+{m}_{21}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{21})+{m}_{12}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{12})+{m}_{22}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{22})+{m}_{13}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{13})+{m}_{23}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{22})
$$

where ${m}_{ij}$ is the *minimum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ We pick the *minimum* value of $f$ because we're finding the *lower* sum.

Taking into account the fact that $\text{Area}({R}_{ij})=1$ for all $6$ subregions, the formula for $L(f,P)$ reduces to

$$
L(f,P)={m}_{11}+{m}_{21}+{m}_{12}+{m}_{22}+{m}_{13}+{m}_{23}.
$$

Now, notice that

- $f(x,y)=x+y$ increases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=x+y$ increases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072149/assets/70e4f9cd213e0dc4429e21cacf5c375d4def1e9ba021f05e45ee6e7820c5ff36.png)

As a result, the *minimum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *smallest* possible $x$ and the *smallest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *bottom left corner* of each subregion.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072149/assets/8135011b8384a668d4bab28282220bb0560e1ae64c2f1d623822435349067f18.png)

Hence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{11} & =f(1,1)=2 \\ {m}_{21} & =f(2,1)=3 \\ {m}_{12} & =f(1,2)=3 \\ {m}_{22} & =f(2,2)=4 \\ {m}_{13} & =f(1,3)=4 \\ {m}_{23} & =f(2,3)=5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}L(f,P) & =2+3+3+4+4+5 \\  & =21.\end{aligned}
$$

Let R=[1,3]×[1,4] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y)=x+y. Further, let P be a partition of R, where

P1={1,2,3},P2={1,2,3,4},P=P1×P2.

Calculate the lower Riemann sum L(f,P).

EXPLANATION

First, let's draw the region R and the partition P.

The lower sum L(f,P) is given by

L(f,P)=m11⋅Area(R11)+m21⋅Area(R21)+m12⋅Area(R12)+m22⋅Area(R22)+m13⋅Area(R13)+m23⋅Area(R22)

where mij is the minimum value of f in each subregion Rij. We pick the minimum value of f because we're finding the lower sum.

Taking into account the fact that Area(Rij)=1 for all 6 subregions, the formula for L(f,P) reduces to

L(f,P)=m11+m21+m12+m22+m13+m23.

Now, notice that

  • f(x,y)=x+y increases as x increases, and

  • f(x,y)=x+y increases as y increases.

As a result, the minimum value of f in each subregion is attained when we have the smallest possible x and the smallest possible y. This is the value at the bottom left corner of each subregion.

Hence:

m11=f(1,1)=2m21=f(2,1)=3m12=f(1,2)=3m22=f(2,2)=4m13=f(1,3)=4m23=f(2,3)=5

Finally,

L(f,P)=2+3+3+4+4+5=21.
